post.title: Sharekey Cryptography Review
post.description: During my master thesis I reviewed the cryptography of the end-to-end encrypted Sharekey collaboration app. This post covers the most interesting issues I found.

post.title: Breaking Military Grade Encryption to Animate my Name
post.description: Getting into the weeds of my flashy website banner, that simulates a padding-oracle attack on AES-CBC.

post.title: Quantum Apocalypse?
post.description: NIST finalized their first post quantum secure cryptographic algorithms in August 2024. This post provides a gentle introduction and an intuition on the actual impact.

post.title: Proton's crypto is not Transparent and not OPAQUE
post.description: Proton says privacy "isn't a promise, it's mathematically ensured." I found new ways they could read your data anyway.
post.keywords: Pascal Schärli, Proton Mail, Key Transparency, end-to-end encryption, cryptography, Proton Pass, electron, Bitwarden

post.title: Post-Quantum Crypto Won't Fix Your Architecture
post.description: Adding PQC to this product was like installing a vault door on a tent. The server could intercept your keys and an RCE let attackers run code on your desktop.
post.keywords: Pascal Schärli, Internxt, Post-Quantum Cryptography, Responsible Disclosure

post.title: Filen's password onion made me cry
post.description: Filen hashes passwords with MD5(MD4(MD2(pwd))). This post shows several cryptographic weaknesses in their protocol and questions if it's even worth doing end-to-end encryption delivered through a webpage.
post.keywords: Pascal Schärli, Filen, MD2, MD4, password hashing, crypto agility, end-to-end encryption, Responsible Disclosure

briefs.title: ETH Study Materials
briefs.description: Welcome to my collection of ETH Zürich study materials. As a former tutor at ETH, I've created resources for two Computer Science courses in the Electrical Engineering and Mechanical Engineering bachelor programs.

briefs.title: When Giants Use Toothpicks
briefs.description: Fireblocks is a digital asset custody platform, protecting trillions of dollars. During a security review at work I found how they protect their 4096-bit RSA 'disaster recovery' keys for customers with 2 rounds of MD5.

briefs.title: What Comes After X.509
briefs.description: X.509 certificates have run the web for three decades. Quantum computers might be what finally kills them. Google announces they don't have immediate plans to add support for post-quantum secure X.509 certificates in Chrome in favor of a newer standard.

briefs.title: 33 Months to Q-Day
briefs.description: The Post-Quantum cryptography timeline of industry leaders just went from "we have a decade" to "we have 33 months." Both Google and Cloudflare are now targeting 2029 for full post-quantum security, including authentication, not just encryption.

briefs.title: Signal adds Key Transparency
briefs.description: Signal Messenger just added Key Transparency (KT) for automatic key verification. It's good but a bit timid. I'm comparing their KT with the one used by Proton, where I disclosed some weaknesses earlier this year.

briefs.title: Electron, we have a problem
briefs.description: Many Electron apps auto-update without verifying signatures. Many also still trust the compromised eMudhra certificates. Together, that lets an attacker on your network install malware on your machine.

page.title: 400 Bad Request
page.description: Your browser said something my server couldn't understand. Awkward silence all around.

page.title: 401 Unauthorized
page.description: This page wants you to prove who you are, but this site doesn't have logins. Something went delightfully sideways.

page.title: 403 Forbidden
page.description: I know exactly who you are, and the answer is still no. Blame me having misconfigured something.

page.title: 404 Not Found
page.description: This page isn't here. Moved, renamed, deleted, or maybe it only ever existed in your imagination.

page.title: 405 Method Not Allowed
page.description: You found the right door, then tried to open it in a way it simply does not open.

page.title: 408 Request Timeout
page.description: The server waited for your request, got bored, and gave up. Reload usually sorts it.

page.title: 429 Too Many Requests
page.description: Woah. That's a lot of requests. Take a breath. Maybe go look at a tree.

page.title: 500 Internal Server Error
page.description: Something broke. My code did something I did not anticipate. It's not you.

page.title: 502 Bad Gateway
page.description: My server asked another server a question and got gibberish back. I messed up my proxy config again.

page.title: 503 Service Unavailable
page.description: The site is temporarily out of order, catching its breath or being tinkered with by me.

page.title: 504 Gateway Timeout
page.description: My server waited for another server that never replied. Probably my puny little server timing out.
